defaults.permitted_development: In Scotland, demolition of a building is generally treated as development. Planning permission is often required unless the demolition falls within a specific exclusion, and listed building or conservation area controls can apply on top.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height right. The key issue is whether the demolition needs planning permission and whether any heritage consent is also required.
rules.depth_rules: There is no depth allowance. Partial demolition and associated rebuilding or structural works are judged on their own facts.
rules.boundary_rules: Hoardings, highway occupation, access arrangements, rubble removal and impacts on adjoining structures are separate regulatory matters alongside the planning decision.
rules.roof_rules: Roof stripping or top-down removal is part of the overall demolition project and should be considered with the full consent position rather than in isolation.
rules.materials_rules: Waste, salvage, asbestos handling and treatment of exposed adjoining surfaces remain important legal duties even where the demolition route itself is clear.

rules.permitted_development: In Scotland, demolition of a building is generally treated as development. Planning permission is often required unless the demolition falls within a specific exclusion, and in denser urban areas the effect on adjoining buildings, street safety and temporary works can be central to the consent route.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height allowance. The main questions are whether planning permission is required and whether listed building or conservation area controls apply.
rules.depth_rules: There is no depth rule. Partial demolition, facade retention and works affecting shared walls or structures are separate planning and structural issues.
rules.boundary_rules: Hoardings, road occupation, rubble removal, craneage and support to adjoining property are separate regulatory matters. Demolition in built-up areas often needs a more managed methodology than the planning label alone suggests.
rules.roof_rules: Roof stripping or top-down demolition is part of the overall demolition proposal and should not be treated separately from the main consent position.
rules.materials_rules: Waste, salvage, asbestos handling and treatment of exposed adjoining surfaces remain important legal duties even where the demolition route itself is clear. In built-up areas, highway safety, party-wall relationships and protection of neighbours usually dominate the practical planning discussion.

restrictions.conservation_area: Demolition in a conservation area can need conservation area consent or associated heritage approvals as well as any planning permission.
restrictions.listed_building: Demolition of a listed building, or of structures protected as part of it, needs listed building consent.
